title: Communication complexity bounded by input sizes
statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite nonempty types, let $\alpha$ be any type, and let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$. Then the deterministic communication complexity of $f$ satisfies
\[
  D(f) \;\le\; \lceil \log_2 \abs{X} \rceil + \lceil \log_2 \abs{Y} \rceil,
\]
where $\abs{X}$ and $\abs{Y}$ denote the cardinalities of $X$ and $Y$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a function X → Y → α
replaced:
For finite, nonempty types $X$ and $Y$ and any function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
the deterministic communication complexity satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{CC}(f) \;\le\; \lceil\log_2 |X|\rceil + \lceil\log_2 |Y|\rceil.
\]
This bound is achieved by the protocol in which Alice sends her entire input to Bob
and Bob then sends his entire input to Alice.
